newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas asks Moslem leaders to ban ties with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hamas asks Moslem leaders to ban ties with Israel.

text.p: The militant Islamic group Hamas appealed on Thursday to Moslem leaders meeting in Morocco to ban normalisation of relations with Israel in an effort to press the Jewish state to stop the "Judaisation" of Jerusalem.

In an open letter addressed to the Jerusalem Committee of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), Hamas said that verbal condemnations were no longer enough to stop Israel from expanding in Arab East Jerusalem at the expense of the Palestinian people.

"The bulldozers of the Zionist occupation are still paving the way to build a settlement on the Palestinian Jabal Abu Ghneim. The Netanyahu government is still challenging the will of the Islamic and Arab world," the letter said.

Israel broke ground last week on the settlement, which it calls Har Homa, plunging Israeli-Palestinian relations into crisis and sparking almost daily clashes between stone-throwing Palestinians and Israeli soldiers.

Palestinians regard East Jerusalem, which Israel annexed after capturing it from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war, as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Israel regards both East and West Jerusalem as its "eternal" capital.

Hamas asked the committee "to take a clear and decisive decision to stop negotiations with the Zionist enemy and to stop all forms of normalisation with it as an expression of rejecting the Zionist settlement and expansion policy."

The 15-member committee, which was set up by an OIC summit in 1975 to fight Israel's "Judaisation" of Jerusalem, was due to meet in Rabat later on Thursday to discuss the planned construction of 6,500 housing units in the new settlement.

Hamas opposes Israeli-PLO peace moves which launched limited Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip and prompted many Arab states to move toward normalisation of ties with the Jewish state.
Hamas suicide bombers have killed scores in attacks in Israeli cities in recent years, including three women in a Tel Aviv cafe last Friday.
